lessons.title: Decompositions & multivariable calculus
lessons.description: Derive the tools behind optimization and representation.
lessons.conceptOverview: SVD factors a matrix into orthogonal directions and singular values. Truncated SVD gives a low-rank approximation. A Jacobian collects first derivatives of vector outputs; a Hessian contains second derivatives of a scalar. Shapes matter when composing derivatives through a neural network.

sections.title: Try it yourself
sections.content: Compute derivatives of a two-variable quadratic and check them using finite differences. Explain what positive Hessian eigenvalues imply locally.

commonMistakes: A Jacobian and Hessian always have the same shape.

lessons.title: Probability & information theory
lessons.description: Derive the tools behind optimization and representation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Maximum likelihood chooses parameters that make observed data probable. Negative log likelihood connects to cross entropy for categorical targets. KL divergence measures a directed discrepancy between distributions and is not symmetric. Mutual information quantifies dependence, rather than causation.

sections.content: Calculate entropy for a fair and a biased binary distribution. Compare KL in both directions and handle zero probabilities explicitly.

lessons.title: Optimization & numerical stability
lessons.description: Derive the tools behind optimization and representation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Floating-point arithmetic rounds values and can overflow or underflow. Stable softmax subtracts the maximum logit before exponentiation. Conditioning describes sensitivity to perturbations; gradient scaling does not fix ill-conditioned data. Compare optimizers using convergence and generalization, not just training loss.

sections.title: Try it yourself
sections.content: Implement stable softmax and test logits near 1000. Verify that probabilities sum to one and remain unchanged when adding the same constant to all logits.

commonMistakes: Exponentiating large logits directly is numerically safe.
